reviewerFeedback:
another layout was rated acceptable: Column 1 gets about 72px, so all store names break 3+2 (上海徐/汇店, 南京新/街口店), cutting place names in half; the resulting two-line blocks are even and the five month columns stay equal and comfortably wide, so numbers scan cleanly, but the row headers are the weak point. | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: Effectively the same as A: identical 3+2 wrapping of store names (杭州西/湖店, 苏州观/前店), even two-line row blocks and even month columns; nothing broken, but row identity is split mid-place-name, which slows reading down the header column. | another layout was rated acceptable: Same 3+2 name wrap as A and B; month columns look evenly proportioned and the numeric grid reads as a clean block, yet the header column still chops 徐汇, 西湖 and 新街口, so the row labels lose a little integrity. | another layout was rated good: The wider header column lets each name put city+district on line one (上海徐汇, 南京新街, 合肥淮河) and isolates the generic suffix 店 on line two, so the distinguishing part stays intact and the lone 店 forms a consistent vertical rhythm; the cost is slightly squeezed month columns (numbers sit closer to the rules) and a stranded single character per row, but the table scans better down the row headers. | another layout was rated poor: The header column is so narrow that names break into three lines (上海/徐汇/店, 南京/新街/口店), producing very tall, airy rows; the whole table becomes a ladder of text with the month figures floating far apart, breaking row cohesion and vertical comparison between months. | another layout was rated acceptable: Same 3+2 split as A/B/C with balanced month columns; readable and consistent, but the row-header breaks fall inside place names (宁波天/一店, 合肥淮/河路店), which is the weakest aspect of an otherwise tidy grid.
another layout was rated poor: 门店 column is only about three characters wide, so every store name splits mid-word (上海徐/汇店, 杭州西/湖店, 苏州观/前店, 宁波天/一店), breaking the branch names readers scan by. The month columns still have spare room that should have gone to column 1. | another layout was rated good: Best balance of the compact layouts: the wider row-header column keeps most branch names intact (上海徐汇/店, 杭州西湖/店), leaving only the trailing 店 orphaned, while all four-digit figures still sit on one line. A few bad splits remain (南京新街/口店), but the table stays compact and scannable. | another layout was rated poor: Same failure as A: three-character header column cuts through branch names (徐/汇, 西/湖, 观/前, 天/一), so row identity is fragmented while the month columns carry unnecessary slack. | another layout was rated poor: Row headers again wrap at three characters, splitting 徐汇, 西湖, 观前 and 天一 across lines; the month columns are wider than the numbers require, so the space is misallocated. | your previous preferred design was rated poor: Visually the same compromise as A/C/D: row labels break inside branch names and the numeric columns keep extra width that column 1 needs more. | another layout was rated acceptable: Two-character breaks give a readable city/branch rhythm (上海/徐汇/店, 苏州/观前/店), but 新街口 and 淮河路 still split badly (口店, 路店), and every row becomes three lines tall. The month columns are clearly over-wide for four-digit numbers, wasting width that could have kept column 1 to two or three clean lines.
